title: LoCoMo 10 — the released dataset, as it actually is
description: The contract for benchmark/locomo/data/locomo10.json. It describes the file as MEASURED, not as the paper describes it: `answer` is optional because 444 of 446 adversarial questions do not carry one, and it is string OR number because six answers are bare integers. A validation failure here means the upstream submodule moved, which is a fact the run must state before it scores anything.

conversation.description: Two speakers, then one `session_<n>` array and one `session_<n>_date_time` string per session. The numbers are the chronological order.

turn.description: `dia_id` is unique WITHIN a sample and repeats across samples — every one of the ten conversations restarts at D1:1 — so an evidence id is only meaningful beside its sample_id.

answer.description: Absent on 444 of the 446 category-5 questions. Six answers across the file are integers rather than strings; the official evaluator coerces with str(), so a port must too.

evidence.description: Dialog ids the answer is grounded in. Not all of them are well formed and not all of them resolve — the loader counts both rather than repairing them.
